title: Tonic-clonic (convulsive)
description: The body may stiffen and then jerk rhythmically. The person is not aware of their surroundings.
first_aid: Stay and time the seizure. Cushion the head and clear nearby hazards; do not restrain the person or put anything in their mouth. When jerking stops, place them on their side if safe. Call emergency services if it lasts 5 minutes or more, repeats without recovery, or they are injured.

title: Absence
description: A brief pause in awareness may look like staring or eyelid fluttering; the person usually resumes what they were doing.
first_aid: Stay nearby and calmly guide the person away from immediate hazards. Reassure them when they become responsive; do not shake or restrain them.

title: Focal aware or impaired awareness
description: A person may have unusual sensations or movements in one area, or become confused and less responsive.
first_aid: Stay with the person and gently guide them away from hazards. Do not restrain them. Time the episode and seek emergency help if it becomes a convulsive seizure lasting 5 minutes or more, repeats without recovery, or causes injury.

title: Myoclonic
description: One or more sudden, brief muscle jerks may happen; awareness is often preserved.
first_aid: Help the person sit or move to a safer place if needed. Do not hold their limbs. Seek medical advice if these episodes are new or changing.

title: Atonic
description: A sudden loss of muscle tone can cause the head to drop or the person to fall.
first_aid: Protect the person from nearby hazards and cushion the head if possible. Check for injury; do not move them if a serious injury is suspected. Call emergency services for injury or breathing concerns.

title: Tonic
description: Muscles suddenly stiffen, sometimes while a person is asleep or standing.
first_aid: Move nearby hazards and protect the head without restraining the person. Time the episode. Afterward, check breathing and place them on their side if safe and needed.
